identity.title: Automated Mining of the ALMA Archive in the COSMOS Field (A<SUP>3</SUP>COSMOS). II. Cold Molecular Gas Evolution out to Redshift 6

paper_type_evidence.quote: Our A$^3$COSMOS dataset contains $\sim700$ galaxies ($0.3 \lesssim z \lesssim 6$) with high-confidence ALMA detections in the (sub-)millimeter continuum and multi-wavelength spectral energy distributions (SEDs).

targets.name: A3COSMOS galaxy sample in the COSMOS field

evidence.quote: a large ($\sim700$), robust galaxy sample at $0.3 < z \lesssim 6$ in the 2 deg$^2$ COSMOS field (cite: Scoville2007) from the A$^3$COSMOS project

distance_source.value: COSMOS spec-z compilation, Laigle2016/Davidzon2017 and Jin2018 photo-z

evidence.quote: a large ($\sim700$), robust galaxy sample at $0.3 < z \lesssim 6$ in the 2 deg$^2$ COSMOS field (cite: Scoville2007) from the A$^3$COSMOS project

question.value: How do the molecular gas depletion time and gas-to-stellar-mass ratio of galaxies depend on stellar mass, offset from the main sequence and cosmic age out to z~6, and what cosmic molecular gas density evolution follows?

evidence.quote: we parameterize galaxies’ molecular gas depletion time ($\tau_{\mathrm{depl}}$) and molecular gas to stellar mass ratio ($\mu_{\mathrm{molgas}}$) each as a function of the stellar mass ($M_{\star}$), offset from the star-forming main sequence ($\Delta{\mathrm{MS}}$) and cosmic age (or redshift).

bands.value: Mostly ALMA Band 6 and 7 (all public archival bands used)

evidence.quote: Our high-redshift galaxies are most commonly observed in ALMA Band 6 and 7
discarded very high resolution (beam size $< 0.1''$) data

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: Public ALMA archival data, release date up to Aug. 1st, 2018

evidence.quote: All A$^3$COSMOS galaxies have robust (sub-)mm continuum detections from public ALMA archival data (release date up to Aug. 1st, 2018)

other_facilities.name: CO-observed literature samples (PHIBSS, xCOLD GASS, etc.)

provided.value: 20 complementary samples of CO-detected galaxies at 0<z<4 for combined fitting

evidence.quote: We include 20 samples of galaxies with CO observations and well-constrained stellar mass and SFR properties from the literature

what.value: A3COSMOS catalog (continuum photometry, MAGPHYS M*, L_IR, Mdust) from the companion paper

evidence.quote: Galaxy properties in the A$^3$COSMOS galaxy catalog, including stellar mass ($M_{\star}$), IR luminosity ($L_{\mathrm{IR}}$) and dust mass ($M_{\mathrm{dust}}$), are obtained from MAGPHYS

evidence.loc: 3.2 Molecular Gas Mass from RJ-tail Dust Continuum

evidence.quote: We use the SIDES mock galaxy catalog and select $\log_{10}M_{\star}>9.0$ star-forming galaxies

what.value: Continuum imaging, photometry extraction, flux bias correction, SED fitting and catalog flags

evidence.quote: We developed pipelines for producing continuum images using nearly all publicly available ALMA archival data in COSMOS
we recalculated all molecular gas masses from the CO line luminosities by applying the metallicity-dependent $\alpha_{\mathrm{CO}}$ following .

ALMA project codes not printed in text

method.value: Apply S/N cuts (5.40 blind, 4.35 prior) and remove flagged sources (inconsistent flux, outlier CPA, outlier SED)

evidence.quote: a peak flux to rms noise ratio of 5.40 for blind extraction and 4.35 for prior photometry

validation.value: Monte Carlo simulations in paper I; spurious fraction near zero

evidence.quote: the spurious fraction is reduced to close to zero according to our statistics in paper

analysis_steps.goal: Compute gas masses via band conversion and RJ-tail calibration

method.value: Scale ALMA flux by MAGPHYS SED ratio Gamma to rest-frame 850 um, compute luminosity, divide by Hughes2017 alpha_850; compare with dust-SED delta_GDR and Groves2015 methods

evidence.quote: then we scale the observed ALMA flux density by $\Gamma^{\mathrm{SED}}$ and compute the luminosity

assumptions.value: Gas mass purely molecular, atomic gas ignored; metallicity from modified Genzel2015 MZR; delta_GDR from Remy-Ruyer2014

evidence.quote: we obtain the dust-SED-based $M_{\mathrm{mol\,gas}}$ by multiplying $M_{\mathrm{dust}}$ with the mass–metallicity-derived $\delta_{\mathrm{GDR}}$ and ignore the contribution from atomic gas

validation.value: Band conversion bias tested with JINGLE galaxies

evidence.quote: we have done some tests using the multi-wavelength data from UV to submm for the JINGLE survey galaxy sample

analysis_steps.goal: Fit functional forms for tau_depl and mu_molgas

method.value: Multivariate fit of log tau_depl and log mu_molgas versus DeltaMS, log M*, cosmic age to combined 1663-galaxy sample; also re-fit Scoville2017 and Tacconi2018 forms

evidence.quote: We use the `Python` packages `pymc3` and `scipy.optimize.curve_fit` for the fitting
In the fitting we allow the coefficients to vary within a relatively large range of $(-10,10)$.

assumptions.value: Speagle2014 MS with cosmic age used for DeltaMS

evidence.quote: Here we adopt the MS function from the #49 fitting of Table 7 of (cite: Speagle2014)
The two algorithms agree very well, and the former one provides better uncertainty estimates for the fitted parameters.

validation.value: chi2 comparison; subsample tests without z>4 and without z>1 CO; alternative gas calibrations

evidence.quote: we tested the stability of our fitting for subsamples of galaxies: (a) only $z<4$ data, and (b) without $z>1$ CO

analysis_steps.goal: Derive cosmic molecular gas mass density

method.value: Sum SMF x M* x mu_molgas for MS galaxies (M*>1e9), and alternative sum over SIDES mock galaxies

evidence.quote: we integrate only down to $M_{\star}=10^{9.0}\;\mathrm{M}_{\odot}$

assumptions.value: SMFs adapted from Peng2010/Davidzon2017 shapes normalized to integrated CSFRD

evidence.quote: we adopt the shape of our SMF from an interpolation of the (cite: Davidzon2017) SMFs

validation.value: Compared to CO blind surveys and SAM of Popping2019

evidence.quote: At higher redshifts ($z>0.5$) our curve coincidentally agrees with the Semi-Analytic Model (SAM) simulation by (cite: Popping2019).

used_for.value: SED fitting for M*, L_IR, Mdust and band conversion

evidence.quote: are obtained from MAGPHYS ((cite: daCunha2008; daCunha2015)) SED fitting
with the FAST ((cite: Kriek2009)) and “SUPER-DEBLENDED” ((cite: Liudz2017; Jin2018)) SED fitting tools
The former package performs Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) fitting to calculate the probability distribution of the fitting
the latter one performs least-chi-square minimization to find the best fit
as automatically determined by the `Python` package `corner`

results_numeric.quantity: reduced chi2 for mu_molgas, this work's form

evidence.quote: In total, we have 1,663 galaxies with redshift, SFR, stellar mass and molecular gas mass measurements.
their $\tau_{\mathrm{depl}}=0.7$, 1.3, 2.6 and 5.0 Gyr, respectively
our SED fitting tends to underestimate their true R-J tail dust continuum by a factor of 2–6

findings_qualitative.value: Functional form implies downsizing and mass-quenching

evidence.quote: implies a “downsizing” effect (i.e., more-massive galaxies evolve earlier than less-massive ones) and “mass-quenching”

claims.hypothesis: Does a new functional form fit gas fraction and depletion time better than Tacconi2018 and Scoville2017 forms?
claims.experiment: Fit three forms to the combined 1663-galaxy sample
claims.result: Reduced chi2 0.86 vs 0.87 (re-fit Tacconi) and 1.26 (re-fit Scoville); original-literature fits worse
claims.finding: The new form is statistically better

evidence.quote: Our proposed functional form provides a statistically better fit to current data (than functional forms in the literature)

claims.hypothesis: Does the gas fraction function reproduce the cosmic molecular gas density to z=6?
claims.experiment: Integrate SMF x mu_molgas and SIDES mock galaxies
claims.result: Agrees with CO blind surveys' upper bounds and SAM of Popping2019
claims.finding: Coherent picture of gas, SFR and stellar mass evolution

evidence.quote: we for the first time infer the cosmic cold molecular gas density evolution out to redshift 6 and find agreement with CO blind surveys as well as semi-analytic modeling

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Lowering S/N threshold to 3.0 doubles sample but 40% spurious

evidence.quote: however 40% of the sample will be spurious based on our simulation statistics

limitations_admitted.value: Band conversion underestimates RJ-tail flux at z>4 lacking long-wavelength data

evidence.quote: it potentially results in a factor of 2–6 underestimation of gas mass at $z>4$

referee_caveats_inferred: Heterogeneous sample, with dust-based gas masses at high z and CO at low z, confounds redshift evolution
Atomic gas ignored and metallicity inferred from relations
MAGPHYS stellar masses 0.25 dex above FAST
